subject: STATISTICS
pageTitle: Probability Rules: And, Or, Independent Events
description: Use the addition and multiplication rules for probability, and know when events are independent or mutually exclusive, with two worked examples.
caption: Probability rules in 7 swipes: AND vs OR, independent vs exclusive, and two worked examples. Save this for your stats quiz. Free Statistics study guide at precisstudy.com/statistics (no sign-up).

slides.title: THE TWO RULES
lines: OR: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B)
AND (independent): P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B)
slides.note: Mutually exclusive events have P(A and B) = 0.

slides.title: TELL THEM APART
lines: Independent: one does not change the other
Mutually exclusive: they cannot both happen
Exclusive events have P(A and B) = 0
slides.note: Independent and mutually exclusive are different ideas.

slides.title: EXAMPLE 1
slides.problem: Flip a coin and roll a die. What is P(heads and a 6)?

slides.title: EXAMPLE 2
slides.problem: P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.25, P(A and B) = 0.1. Find P(A or B).

slides.title: WATCH OUT
slides.wrong: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) always
points: You must subtract P(A and B) so the overlap is not counted twice.
Only mutually exclusive events skip the subtraction.
